review.alternative: Autonomous agents might circumvent recurrence limitations through unbounded non-parametric memory storage.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that memory retention overhead does not scale with trajectory complexity in optimal first-order methods.

claims.statement: Constant-memory first-order methods and oracle complexity constraints establish explicit lower bounds on how historical trajectory information restricts future optimization paths.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that recurrence and constant-memory constraints strictly bound optimization convergence, mirroring memory limits on preference acquisition.
support.passage: The proof constructs an explicit hard instance for the lower bound and a constant-memory first-order method, ITEM-wf (previously called ITEM-w), whose worst-case performance matches this lower bound.

actions.findings: Constant-memory first-order methods and oracle complexity constraints establish explicit lower bounds on how historical trajectory information restricts future optimization paths. [source-8f2756c55be14a96]
actions.limitations: Formal bounds are established for constrained convex optimization models rather than arbitrary neural architectures.
actions.next_questions: How do first-order method recurrence bounds map to empirical memory retention limits in large-scale autonomous architectures?
actions.reason: Revising the foundational memory preference notebook with newly verified recurrence and oracle complexity source data.
actions.summary: Revised analysis integrating recurrence bounds and exact convex minimax risk formulations into the understanding of how memory constraints restrict autonomous preference evolution.
actions.title: Path-Dependent Inference and Memory Constraints in Preference Acquisition
